about.what: Reference labels for the 8 rewritten facts of the fresh 2b run of 2026-11-12 on lectures 1, 4 and 16 (Sage judge, Qwen rewrites; the run kept in analysis/fact_extraction/data/history/2b_2026-11-12_fresh_sage/). Labelled by Fable on 2026-11-15 against the segment transcripts and the eight properties of pipeline/prompts/fact_judge.txt as revised after gate review 1 (changes 1 to 7).
about.fields: The key is the fact's ID among that run's final facts, not a 2a ID: after a split or a removal the numbers shift, so 1/S3/F6 here is not the 2a fact 1/S3/F6. rewrite_of: the 2a fact it was rewritten from. evidence, text: as the rewrite gave them (evidence as sentence IDs). pass, fails, borderline, note: as in gold.json (1 Significant, 2 Whole, 3 Established, 4 Grounded, 5 Self-contained, 6 Terms in full, 7 On the subject, 8 Faithful). Each fact is judged within the final facts of its segment, so Whole is checked against the kept facts and the other rewrites.
about.caveats: One labeller. From the run only the rewritten texts and their evidence were taken; its judgements, the problems given to the rewrite and the verdicts of the rejudge were not read. Not fully blind: the review (reviews/review_1_2026-11-13.md) says which two rewrites the old judge failed again and gives the reviewer's reading of three of them. The rewrites of a later run have other texts: label them anew, do not reuse these labels by ID.
about.counts: 8 rewrites of 7 facts: 5 pass, 3 fail, 1 borderline.

1/S0/F1.text: Extended reality (XR), virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and mixed reality (MR) can refer to different things to different people: for some, magical movie scenes; for some, three-dimensional (3D) or four-dimensional (4D) movie-theater documentaries about extinct animals; and, for virtual reality (VR), the most common perception is that a user wears a headset that blocks vision and is transported to a virtual world.
1/S0/F1.note: Still the summary of the segment's motivating examples, cut from six to three (64 words). Properties 1 and 3: the movie scenes and the documentaries are associations the lecturer raises only to ask whether they are what the terms mean ('But is it really the only thing', sentence 48; 'But is that so?', sentence 58), and he teaches neither. Property 2: it holds the remark that the terms mean different things to different people, two such associations, and the headset (sentences 59-61), which is the one teachable point and should be a fact of its own (worn on the head, blocks vision, the most common perception of VR); removing the whole fact would lose it. Property 6 is now met ('three-dimensional (3D) or four-dimensional (4D)'). Each part is found in the cited sentences. Labelled like the 2a fact in gold.json, without 6.

1/S3/F4.text: The term metaverse has heavily stimulated and spurred growth in the extended reality field.
1/S3/F4.note: One point, grounded and faithful ('heavily' is kept; 'the field' of sentence 182 is the extended reality field). The rewrite dropped 'in use for more than 30 years' (sentence 181), which the 2a fact held and which was not a failure: this fact passes, but it is poorer than the 2a fact and no fact holds the age of the term now.

1/S3/F5.text: The metaverse is not merely an application of virtual reality, mixed reality, or augmented reality technology.
1/S3/F5.note: One half of a split: it says only what the metaverse is not. The other half is F6 (what it is, on one view). The 2a fact 1/S3/F5 held both and was the better fact. F5 and F6, with F7 as the detail of F6, are one point.

1/S3/F6.text: One broad point of view about the metaverse is that humans are going to reimagine the way they interact with the digital world.
1/S3/F6.note: The other half of the split (see F5), and the same point as F7 (the 2a fact 1/S3/F6, kept): 'reimagine the way they interact with the digital world' says nothing until F7 says how (acting as in the real world, natural interaction in an all-around three-dimensional environment instead of flat screens). Faithful to sentence 185 otherwise.

4/S1/F0.text: A system can be categorized as a virtual reality (VR) system and distinguished from other systems when it has the three characteristics of an artificial environment, sensory experience by computer-generated stimuli, and user actions that partially determine what happens in the environment.
4/S1/F0.note: One statement now: when a system counts as a virtual reality system, naming the three characteristics without describing them. The second assertion of the 2a fact ('other systems, which are not supposed to have these aspects') is gone, and the fact has 42 words for 57. Borderline: it still carries the use of the list ('categorized ... and distinguished from other systems'), the point of 4/S2/F0 in the next segment, so a reader who fails the 2a fact for holding the list and its use can fail this one in the same way; the cleanest fact is the list alone. Grounded in sentences 34, 36-38 and 57.

4/S1/F3.text: The sensory experience characteristic of a virtual reality (VR) system is that the system provides computer-generated stimuli to the user's sensory organs, such as eyes and ears, so the user can immersively experience the artificial or synthetic environment, and immersive experience is a hallmark of a virtual reality system.
4/S1/F3.note: The 2a fact with 'this immersive experience' written as 'immersive experience' (the code check's false alarm) and 'means that' as 'is that'; nothing lost. One point, grounded in sentences 57-60 and 62.

16/S1/F9.text: In virtual reality (VR), tracking the surrounding environment can alert the user to physical objects not represented in the virtual world, such as a wall, to reduce harm; for alerting the user to physical objects not represented in the virtual world, tracking the user is not useful, and the surrounding environment must be tracked.
16/S1/F9.note: The 2a fact with 'for this' spelled out (the code check's false alarm): 'physical objects not represented in the virtual world' is now said twice, so the fact is clumsier than the 2a fact, but it is one point and faithful ('can alert' for 'may alert', sentence 49; 'not useful' for 'will not be of any use', sentence 55).

16/S1/F11.text: In applications such as telepresence, a large part of the physical world can be brought into the virtual world through live capture; augmenting the virtual world with a live capture of the real world is generally classified as augmented virtuality and is a form of tracking the surrounding environment.
16/S1/F11.note: The 2a fact with 'this is generally classified' spelled out (the code check's false alarm). 'generally' is kept, and 'a form of' for 'some sort of' (sentence 61) is acceptable. That the live capture counts as augmented virtuality is a new statement about live capture, not a recap, though the lecturer recalls the term from the introductory lectures.

neighbours.1/S3/F7: A kept fact (the 2a fact 1/S3/F6, gold pass). After the split of 1/S3/F5 it is the same point as the rewrite 1/S3/F6: a judge that fails it for Whole together with F6 is right, and that counts against the rewrite, not against the judge.
